title: Backfill incident_type for last 90 days (incident-bot + postmortems) to validate v1 taxonomy + baseline metrics
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
Goal
- Perform a one-time backfill of incident_type + subtype for the last 90 days of incidents (customer-impacting + high-severity internal incidents) using the v1 taxonomy.
- Use this to: (1) validate the taxonomy is usable under real incident pressure, (2) establish baseline incident volume by type/owner, (3) identify “unknown/unclassified” drivers and taxonomy ambiguity before we enforce required classification in tooling.

Scope
- Time window: last 90 days from 2025-12-10 (rolling window used for analysis; lock window on export date).
- Data sources:
  1) incident-bot incidents (Slack #incidents + incident-bot records)
  2) Postmortems (Confluence + links from incident-bot)
  3) Support escalations that were handled as incidents (best-effort cross-link via Jira IDs when present)
- Out of scope: creating new taxonomy categories during backfill. If we hit missing categories, log as “taxonomy_gap” notes for v1.1 discussion.

Outputs / Deliverables
- Backfill sheet (Drive): incident_id, start_time, end_time, severity, tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), affected_region, primary incident_type, subtype, primary_owner (per mapping table), secondary/contributing systems, confidence (high/med/low), notes, links (Slack channel, postmortem, Jira).
- Summary report (Confluence comment or short write-up linked from this ticket):
  - counts by incident_type/subtype
  - counts by owner team
  - % unknown/unclassified and top reasons
  - top 5 recurring incident types by tier
  - proposed decision-tree clarifications (no taxonomy churn inside this ticket; just recommendations)

Classification rules (apply consistently)
- Choose a single primary incident_type/subtype even when there are multiple contributing factors.
  - If multiple causes, pick the earliest/most-direct customer-impact driver as primary type; list other drivers in “contributing systems/notes.”
- If ambiguous between two types and evidence is insufficient, set type to “unknown/unclassified” and add a short note describing what was missing (e.g., “no router fallback_reason emitted”, “no client vs gateway breakdown”).
- Use v1 definitions exactly; do not invent subtypes.
- Owner should be resolved from the v1 ownership mapping table; if mapping is unclear, set owner to “unresolved” and tag for follow-up.

Acceptance Criteria
- Backfill completed for all Sev0/Sev1 incidents in window; Sev2+ included where data is available (target: >= 90% coverage overall).
- >= 95% of backfilled incidents have a non-empty incident_type (including unknown/unclassified).
- Summary report posted with baseline metrics + recommended tweaks to definitions/decision tree.
- At least 1 review pass completed by SRE + one domain reviewer (Routing/Fleet/Runtime) for spot checks.

Implementation plan
1) Export list of incidents for last 90 days (incident-bot) with severity/tier/links.
2) Gather postmortem metadata for incidents that have them; attach links.
3) Perform initial classification pass using v1 taxonomy definitions + decision tree.
4) Spot-check and adjudicate disputed categories in a short async review:
   - Routing/Fallback vs Fleet/Capacity
   - Runtime regression vs telemetry false positive
   - Client/network vs gateway for streaming disconnects
5) Freeze dataset (date-stamped), compute summary pivots, and publish results.

Links
- Taxonomy v1 definitions: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-taxonomy-v1-definitions.json
- Ownership + remediation SLA matrix: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-ownership-mapping-and-remediation-sla-matrix.json
- Working analysis doc (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/top-incidents-analysis-last-2-quarters.json
- Backfill sheet (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/classification-backfill-sheet-last-90-days.json

Notes / Risks
- Data quality: a subset of incidents lack explicit tier or clean end_time; we’ll use incident-bot timestamps and add “data_gap” notes.
- Avoid high-cardinality labels: do not add freeform categories; keep strictly to v1.
- This backfill is used to calibrate dashboard metrics; ensure any “unknown/unclassified” is explicitly counted and not dropped.
comments: 2025-12-11 — Mei Lin: Pulled incident-bot export for 2025-09-11 → 2025-12-10. Total incidents: 67 (Sev0/1: 14, Sev2+: 53). Missing tier field for 9 incidents; will infer from affected services + customer list where possible and mark as “tier_unknown” when not.

2025-12-12 — Allison Grant: Please keep “unknown/unclassified” as a single bucket (don’t create multiple unknown sub-reasons as separate subtypes). Put unknown reasons in notes only to avoid cardinality problems when we later plumb this into metrics.

2025-12-13 — Sofia Ivanova: For runtime regressions, prefer mapping to runtime subtypes (OOM/KV cache thrash/scheduler stall) only if we have the runtime signals or clear postmortem evidence. Otherwise keep at “Runtime regression (unspecified)” and note missing signals; we’ll use this to justify adding signals for auto-suggest.

Two were reclassified from “Capacity shortage” → “Routing/fallback misbehavior” based on evidence of policy misrouting (fallback_reason=policy) causing unnecessary failover loops. Please list Fleet as contributing system where saturation existed but wasn’t the trigger.

Agree on primary “Capacity/fleet shortage” for 2, and “Routing/fallback misbehavior” for 1 where capacity was available but routing constraints pinned to an unhealthy pool.
